name: Gabriel Tennant
languages: French (from the Illinois river towns, where his mother's family came from)
equipment: Leather duster over a leather blacksmith's apron, a grey flannel shirt and a black preacher's coat for Sundays
Navy revolver (Colt 1851 pattern, .36, cap-and-ball), 6 chambers loaded, which he carries because the road is the road and has never fired at a man
Pick handle, which in his hands is a hammer handle from his own forge
A Bible, worn soft, with the names of his mother, father and four sisters written in the front, and the free papers his father carried in Illinois folded inside the back cover
Smith's hammer and tongs, and a set of horseshoes and nails
His forge account book: every horse he has shod in Ninebark since June, by owner, date and shoe; Fiddler's Station's string is shod by him, with a toe clip of his own pattern
Horse: Moses, a heavy black draught horse who pulls Gabriel's wagon and will carry him at a walk
features: Hard Country (Frontier-Born origin: advantage on saves against exhaustion from heat, cold, thirst and hard travel; once per long rest he can shrug off a level of exhaustion gained on the trail)

Fire and Brimstone (Preacher, using WIS: as an action he preaches. Steady: allies within 30 ft who hear him gain 1d6 + 3 temporary hit points and end frightened and Shaken. Shake: enemies within 30 ft make a WIS save, DC 13, or are frightened of him until the end of his next turn. 3 uses per short rest. No miracles: only a big man's voice and the fact that people believe him)

Comfort the Afflicted (Preacher: he stabilizes a dying creature as a bonus action with a DC 10 Medicine check, and it regains 1 hit point; ten minutes with someone grieving, frightened or ashamed ends their Shaken condition and tells him what truly troubles them; once per short rest, from Shepherd)

The Flock (Preacher, 2nd level: wherever there is a church, a camp meeting or decent people he finds shelter, a meal, news and someone to speak for him; once per town, an hour's preaching gives +1 Reputation there, or -1 to someone he preaches against by name)

Calling: Shepherd (Preacher, 3rd level: Steady also gives each ally advantage on its next attack roll or saving throw before the end of its next turn, and Comfort the Afflicted can be used once per short rest)
Ability Score Improvement (Preacher, 4th level: +2 Strength; twenty years at a forge)

Every Horse Comes Through (Blacksmith background: he can tell a horse's owner, how far it has come and how hard it was ridden from its shoes, and reads a horseshoe track like a signature, especially his own)

personality.traits: I am slow to speak and slower to anger, and when I do speak I preach a little, which I know and do not apologise for. I sing at the forge. I look a man in the eye.
personality.ideals: Thou shalt not kill is not a suggestion, and it has no exception for committees.
personality.bonds: My forge on Water Street, which I built with my own hands and is the first thing I have ever owned. The Methodist class meeting I lead on Sunday evenings in Moira Kehoe's front room, eleven souls. And Jack Tillery, God help him, whom I sat with the last night, and who asked me to tell the truth for him.
personality.flaws: I know exactly what this camp would do to a Black man who accused one of its first citizens, and I have let that knowledge keep me quiet for three weeks. Fear is a sin I have not yet repented of.

appearance: A huge, deep-chested Black man of thirty-six with a short greying beard, a shaved head, burn scars on both forearms, a deep, slow, resonant voice and a surprising gentleness of hand. Leather apron at the forge, black coat on Sunday, a wide-brimmed black hat always.
backstory: Gabriel Tennant was born free in 1828 on a farm outside Alton, Illinois, the son of a man who had bought his own freedom in Missouri and walked across the river with the papers in his shirt. He was apprenticed to a blacksmith at twelve and licensed as a Methodist exhorter at twenty-five, and in 1859 he went to Colorado with a freighting outfit to shoe its oxen, and on to the new camps in 1863. In Ninebark he has the busiest forge in the gulch: he shoes the express company's horses, the stage station's, the packers' mules and half the miners'. On the night of 5 November the committee, wanting a preacher at the hanging and finding no other willing, sent for him to sit with Jack Tillery. Tillery told him, near dawn: 'The man said I'd live if I gave the names he gave me. He lied, didn't he, Reverend.' Gabriel did not see who the man was. He told the committee's president, Obadiah Wexford, who told him to keep it to himself 'for his own sake'. He has.

dmNotes.roleplaying: Gabriel is the campaign's conscience and its most important witness, and he knows both things and is frightened of both. Play him as a big, kind, slow, immovable man who has decided that he will not let another man hang without speaking, and who needs the party to make speaking survivable. He will stand between a mob and a prisoner, Bible in one hand and nothing in the other. He will not take a life.
dmNotes.voice: Deep, slow, a southern Illinois cadence with the rhythm of the pulpit in it. Uses scripture the way other men use proverbs, briefly and to the point. Calls men 'brother' and women 'sister' once he trusts them, and 'sir' and 'ma'am' until then.
dmNotes.motivations: Primary: tell the truth about what Tillery said, and live. Secondary: protect his class meeting, especially Moira Kehoe. Tertiary: keep his forge; it is everything he owns.
dmNotes.secrets: Gabriel holds two clues. CLUE B1: Tillery's last words, about 'the man' who gave him names. CLUE D2: he shoes Fiddler's Station's horses with a toe clip of his own pattern, and he will recognise those shoes in the tracks at the robbery site on the Rattlesnake Grade if anyone brings him a track, a cast shoe or a drawing (vg-scenario-001 or 002). He has not put the two together, because he likes Warrick Sefton, who pays on time and calls him Mister Tennant. He also knows that Sefton stood the guard on Tillery on the night of 5 November, because Sefton let him in.
dmNotes.attitude: Toward the party: courteous and watchful; warms quickly to anyone who protects someone weaker. Toward the committee: grief and contempt. Toward Sefton: friendly, unsuspecting, until the party gives him reason. Toward Moira Kehoe: pastoral and protective. Toward Barnabas Wyndham: respect. Toward Konrad Kranzler, if he is played: a kindred spirit; they argue about God.
